summary: With a string search value, replace substitutes only the first matching occurrence and returns a new string.
documentation: With a string search value, replace substitutes only the first matching occurrence and returns a new string. A replacement function can return literal text without interpreting dollar-sign substitution patterns in the replacement value.
inputs: An object with text, needle and replacement strings; needle is nonempty.
returns: The string after one literal replacement, or the original when absent.
caution: A replacement string interprets tokens such as $&. This exercise treats replacement text literally by returning it from a function. replaceAll would change too many occurrences.
scenarios: Replace one placeholder in a preview while leaving later copies visible.
Edit the first occurrence of a label in a local template.
Apply one literal substitution supplied by a user without dollar-token expansion.
title: Replace one occurrence literally
problem: Replace only the first exact, case-sensitive occurrence of needle in text with the literal replacement value. Treat dollar signs and backslashes as ordinary replacement characters. Needle is nonempty.
hint: Pass a function returning replacement as the second argument.
goal: Use String.replace() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
